purpose: Liraglutide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults and children with type 2 diabetes, and it may also lower the risk of serious heart problems in people who already have heart disease. Under the brand name Saxenda, it is also used to help with weight loss in people who are overweight or obese. It works best when combined with healthy eating and regular exercise.
how_it_works: Liraglutide mimics a natural hormone in your body called GLP-1, which is released after you eat. It tells your pancreas to release insulin when your blood sugar is high, helps stop your liver from releasing too much sugar, and slows down how quickly food leaves your stomach so you feel full longer. Think of it as helping your body respond to food in a more balanced and controlled way.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, and stomach upset, especially when you first start the medication. You may also notice a decrease in appetite or a slight increase in heart rate. These effects often get better after the first few weeks as your body adjusts.
warnings: This medication carries a warning about a possible risk of a rare type of thyroid tumor called medullary thyroid carcinoma, so it should not be used if you or a family member has had this type of thyroid cancer. It can also cause inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis), so tell your doctor right away if you have severe stomach pain that does not go away. Do not use this medication if you are pregnant, and always tell your doctor about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: Liraglutide is given as a once-daily injection just under the skin, usually in your stomach, thigh, or upper arm. For diabetes (Victoza), the starting dose is typically 0.6 mg once daily for one week, then increased to 1.2 mg, and possibly up to 1.8 mg if needed. For weight loss (Saxenda), the dose starts low and is gradually increased over several weeks up to 3 mg once daily. Your doctor will guide you through the dose increases.
